title: ABACUS: A Benchmark for Image Editing Models to Assess Object Category and Counting Under Scene Conservation
abstract: arXiv:2610.28316v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Instruction-based image editing models can now add, remove a specified number of objects or change their category while preserving the scene. Yet these models often fail to produce the correct number, and these failures grow sharply as scenes become more complex and the requested count increases. Current benchmarks largely miss this problem: they score edits with holistic similarity metrics or with vision-language model (VLM) judges that are themselves poor at counting, so numerical errors go unnoticed or are graded incorrectly. As a result, the true numerical ability of today's editing models has never been accurately measured. We address this issue with ABACUS, a new benchmark, evaluation protocol and dedicated scoring metric for numerical image editing. Our protocol is judge-free: no VLM or MLLM scores an edit or counts objects (a VLM only confirms the category of rare ambiguous crops). Instead, it verifies each edit at the instance

translated_title: ABACUS：一个用于评估图像编辑模型在场景保持下对象类别与计数能力的基准
translated_abstract: 基于指令的图像编辑模型如今可以在保持场景不变的情况下添加、移除指定数量的对象或更改其类别。然而，这些模型往往无法生成正确的数量，并且随着场景变得更加复杂和所要求的数量增加，这些失败急剧增多。当前的基准测试在很大程度上忽视了这一问题：它们使用整体相似度指标或本身不擅长计数的视觉语言模型（VLM）评判者来评估编辑结果，因此数值错误要么未被察觉，要么被错误评分。结果，当今编辑模型的真实数值能力从未被准确测量。我们通过ABACUS来解决这一问题，这是一个针对数值图像编辑的新基准、评估协议和专用评分指标。我们的协议是无评判者的：没有任何VLM或多模态大语言模型（MLLM）对编辑结果进行评分或计算对象数量（VLM仅用于确认少数模糊裁剪图像的类别）。相反，它在实例级别验证每次编辑。
tldr: ABACUS是一个针对图像编辑模型数值能力的新基准，采用无VLM评判的评估协议和专用评分指标，首次准确测量了模型在保持场景的同时添加、移除或更改对象类别与数量的真实能力。
en_tdlr: ABACUS is a new benchmark with a judge-free evaluation protocol and dedicated scoring metric that, for the first time, accurately measures image editing models' true numerical ability to add, remove, or change the category and count of objects while preserving the scene.
